title: A locally finitely presented universal single-direct-image rank representative
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be flat, proper and locally of finite presentation, and let $E,F$ be finite locally free modules [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] on $X$. There are a scheme $W$ and an immersion $j:W\to S$ locally of finite presentation such that every $g:T\to S$ factors through $j$ if and only if $\mathrm{PicardUniversalSingleRankMatch}(f,E,F,g)$ [def-sc-picard-universal-single-rank-match]. There is no structure-sheaf unit or connected-fibre assumption; only the ordinary direct image of $F$ is tested.

proof.text: The clopen rank-r locus X_r of E and its complement have clopen images because f is open and closed. In V=f(X), define S_r=V minus f(X minus X_r). These disjoint clopen components are precisely the nonempty homogeneous-rank fibres. A mixed fibre has an open neighbourhood in the images of two distinct rank loci, meeting none of the S_r. The complement of V is clopen and has empty inverse image. The residue-field tests in the single-image condition force every test map into the union of these homogeneous and empty components; two distinct ranks persist after field extension.

On each S_r, F is finitely presented and relatively flat. The perfect direct-image/base-change theorem gives perfect Rf_*F with arbitrary derived base change. Its derived pullbacks have no negative cohomology. A finite strictly perfect model therefore locally has Tor amplitude [0,b].

Apply the universal lowest-cohomology locus theorem in degree zero and rank r. The H^0 derived-base-change comparison identifies its universal fixed-rank condition with the ordinary direct image of F after every further base change. Reference E has rank r on the entire inverse image. Nonempty fibres make every local reference-rank witness equal r by stalk rank, so local finite freeness is exactly the single-image condition, also for nonreduced tests.

The chart immersions agree uniquely on overlaps, and these identifications satisfy the cocycle condition because immersions are monomorphisms. Glue them on each S_r and take their disjoint union with the empty-fibre component. The union is locally an immersion over S, or empty near mixed fibres, and local finite presentation is local on the target. Test factors glue uniquely. On empty fibres both F direct image and its restrictions are zero, and the reference rank clause is vacuous, so rank zero works. Empty test schemes are vacuous; rank zero on nonempty fibres is covered by the same lowest-cohomology construction.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_picardUniversalSingleRankLocus_finitePresentation
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (E F : X.Modules) [E.IsFiniteLocallyFree] [F.IsFiniteLocallyFree] :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (j : W ⟶ S),
      IsImmersion j ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation j ∧
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S),
        (∃ h : T ⟶ W, h ≫ j = g) ↔ PicardUniversalSingleRankMatch f E F g
